testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Lift the brake pedal toward them.

questions.explanation: To stop an air-braked vehicle normally, press down the brake pedal and control the pressure for a smooth, safe stop.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located ____ a brake drum.
questions.explanation: The braking mechanisms that stop the vehicle are located inside the brake drum.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: If you don't drain air tanks, what could happen?

options.text: Water could freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water could freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.

questions.question: If spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.
Open the door to the cab.

questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. Using both springs and air pressure together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are used:

options.text: On all wheels of a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all wheels of a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are used on every wheel of a vehicle. The most common type is the s-cam drum brake.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer doesn't, what happens?

options.text: ABS will still help you steer better.
ABS will make your brake lights brighter.

questions.correctAnswerText: ABS will still help you steer better.
questions.explanation: If only your tractor has ABS, it will still improve steering control. Watch your trailer and ease off the brakes if it starts to swing.

questions.question: With manually operated tank drains, how often should you drain them?
questions.explanation: With manually operated drains, drain the air tanks at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: An air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When air is pumped into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air is pumped into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: What is true about vehicles with dual air brake systems?

options.text: They have air pressure in the brakes even when the engine is off.
They keep some air pressure in the brakes when the engine is off.
The engine must run to build air pressure so the brakes work properly.
They keep air pressure for up to four hours after the engine is shut off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine must run to build air pressure so the brakes work properly.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, run the engine to let the air compressor build pressure. You need at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary brake systems.

questions.question: When you push the brake pedal, how do air brakes respond?

options.text: Only when it is warm outside.

questions.explanation: Air brakes do not work instantly. Air takes time to travel through the lines to reach the brakes. There is usually a delay of at least half a second between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?

options.text: Lower the windows in the cab.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: When leaving a vehicle unattended, what should a driver do?

options.text: Only set the parking brake if parked on a slope.
Let 10 percent of air out of the tires.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: They should not be used in cold weather.
They remove water and oil from the air tanks.
They send air to the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air usually contains water and oil. These can harm the brake system if they build up. Air tanks have drain valves to help remove water and oil.

questions.question: What can happen if you do not drain the air brake tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained to remove water and oil buildup. If water builds up, it can freeze in cold weather and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: What does the air compressor do in a truck's air brake system?

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks in an air brake system. The air compressor governor controls the compressor.

questions.question: How should air tank drains be used?

options.text: The driver should not use them.
Use them only when it is wet outside.
Use them to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use them to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil that can damage the brakes if they build up. You should open the air tank drains every day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems make too much noise.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: When used and maintained properly, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes used?

options.text: Only at the driver's side wheels.

questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are used at each wheel. The most common type is the S-cam drum brake.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how long should it take air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi?
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems in about 45 seconds.

questions.question: What kind of brakes do most newer heavy-duty trucks use?
questions.explanation: Most newer heavy-duty trucks use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems that work with one set of brake controls.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?
questions.explanation: Air brakes work by using compressed air.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 3 psi of air pressure in one minute during a leakage test.
